battlecards.why_selected: Agreed to national pricebook with locked pricing and a rich back-end rebate ($297K) plus front-end price improvements, delivering the best total economics while avoiding costly equipment transitions.
battlecards.contract_terms: National Rebate & Pricebook Agreement executed 9/25/2025; pricing holds until written notice; rebates paid quarterly; term aligned to calendar year with renewal by mutual consent.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Threat of shifting volume to competing OEMs, bundled spend across multiple BUs, and detailed benchmark analysis showing Carrier price gaps.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Broad product line; nationwide parts network; willingness to lock pricing and offer aggressive rebates.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Price competitiveness on certain parts SKUs remains below Daikin benchmarks.
battlecards.switching_costs: Technician training, inventory of proprietary parts, and warranty considerations tied to Carrier equipment.
battlecards.notes: Q3 rebate audit underway to confirm ≥$102K back-end payment.

battlecards.why_not_selected: Front-end pricing not competitive with other OEMs; agreement and potential signing bonus still under negotiation.
battlecards.contract_terms: Draft proposal: tiered rebate (16–20%) back to dollar one; agreement not yet signed.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Ability to shift Carrier/Daikin volume and require Lennox to match competitive price targets.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Attractive 16% base rebate; strong brand recognition.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Higher unit prices on like-for-like SKUs vs market; limited flexibility on front-end discounts.
battlecards.switching_costs: Would require re-tooling install standards and technician certifications.
battlecards.notes: Treya awaiting Lennox BAFO including proposed signing bonus.

battlecards.why_selected: 8% national rebate versus 6.5% under Gemaire, standardized net pricing across all dealer partners, and growth tiers up to 16%.
battlecards.contract_terms: Consolidator Incentive Agreement effective 1/1/2026; 1-year incentive term with renewal by mutual agreement; rebates paid quarterly and tied to aggregated dealer spend.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Aggregated multi-brand spend presented to Rheem; willingness to sign national agreement before year-end.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Nationwide distribution footprint; clear rebate ladder; consistent pricing.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Limited front-end price concessions—savings driven primarily by back-end rebate.
battlecards.switching_costs: Onboarding new distributors and updating purchasing systems across five BUs.

battlecards.why_not_selected: Could not match improved 8% rebate and unified pricing offered directly by Rheem.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Established local relationships and inventory availability.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Lower rebate (6.5%) and fragmented pricing across regions.
battlecards.switching_costs: Minimal—same OEM product line; transition largely administrative.
complexity_reasons: Supplier displaced due to national agreement

battlecards.why_selected: Met target pricing on key SKUs and accepted 2% 10-day discount; agreed to hold margins for new acquisitions.
battlecards.contract_terms: MOU 1/20/2026; term 1/1/2026–12/31/2026; 30-day notice for price increases; 2% discount if paid by 10th.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Competitive multi-round RFP with price targets and SKU-level benchmarking.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Strong inventory levels; willingness to standardize national pricing.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Quoted only 24% of SKUs; reliant on manufacturer price increases.
battlecards.switching_costs: Low—commoditized products; main risk is delivery lead time during transition.

battlecards.why_selected: Delivered best total savings in Round 2, reversing an initial $79K deficit to a $26K gain.
battlecards.contract_terms: MOU 1/20/2026; 1-year term with option to renew; pricing subject to 30-day notice.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Ability to shift volume toward winning distributor; clearly defined target prices for high-spend SKUs.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Responsive price adjustments between rounds; regional branch support.
complexity_reasons: Meaningful turnaround between R1 and R2

battlecards.why_selected: Improved pricing on 92 SKUs (largest coverage) and aligned to target benchmarks though net savings were modest.
battlecards.contract_terms: MOU 1/20/2026; 1-year term; 30-day notice on increases; early-pay terms mirror incumbents.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: High SKU coverage positioned Baker as hedge against Hughes/R.E. Michel pricing.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Broad catalogue; competitive on thermostat and filter SKUs.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Still negative $7K savings in Round 2; may need future true-up.
battlecards.switching_costs: Low; similar freight network to peers.

battlecards.why_not_selected: Could not achieve target pricing; did not submit competitive Round 2 proposal.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Large branch network, broad SKU availability.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Highest unit prices on benchmark SKUs, negative savings in R1 analysis.

battlecards.why_selected: Rampart GPO program delivered 43% savings and simplified contract management across all BUs.
battlecards.contract_terms: GPO master agreement; implementation timeline 3–4 months; consolidated rental program.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Ability to shift 83% of spend away from Cintas; aggregated headcount across 7 BUs.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Competitive rental rates; scalable program; existing relationships with two BUs.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Longer rollout (3–4 months); limited local stock in some regions.
battlecards.switching_costs: Pickup of existing Cintas inventory; re-measuring technicians.

battlecards.why_not_selected: Pricing 12–56% higher than Unifirst across BUs; unwilling to match GPO rates.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Established service routes; existing contracts with majority of BUs.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: High rental rates; inconsistent discounts; complicated rebate structures.
battlecards.switching_costs: Return of rented garments and lockers; contract termination fees if any.
